sampling_model.design: Independent superpopulation sampling under conditional unconfoundedness; identification of \(\Delta(\tau)\) is taken as given, and the contribution is noncritical row-wise limit and inference theory.
sampling_model.units: \(O_i=(X_i,A_i,Y_i)\), \(i=1,\ldots,n\), with a finite reported quantile set \(\mathcal T\).
sampling_model.treatment: Treatment is binary and the two fitted probabilities are generated by one joint log odds, so they sum to one pointwise. Heavy and finite-variance labels remain population regimes separated from \(\gamma=2\) only in the intended downstream theory.
sampling_model.overlap: Positivity holds almost surely. Heavy arms have a common uniform second-order Hall lower-tail expansion. Finite-inverse-moment arms with finite \(\gamma_a\) inherit a uniform Lindeberg bound from Hall tails and gamma separation, while \(\gamma_a=\infty\) arms have a common propensity lower bound from the fixed Hölder ball.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Each fold now fits one constrained and ridged logistic series with clipped log coordinates for both endpoints, setting \(\widehat\pi_{0,-k}=1-\widehat\pi_{1,-k}\). On the explicit mixed chart, sample-point consistency of the bounded arm is proved under \(J_n^{5/2}(\log n)^3/n\to0\) and \(J_n^{-s}\log n\to0\). No uniform rate over the full frozen smooth class is claimed.

body.tldr: The binary propensity model and learner are repaired as one endpoint-safe joint logistic series fit, whose score is \((A-\pi_1)v\) and whose information is \(E_P(\pi_0\pi_1vw)\). The mixed and two-heavy examples remain in the model, and bounded-control clipping and classification are proved on the mixed chart under the corrected joint-fit schedule. The frozen class, however, does not regularize the chart maps enough to prove the uniform profiled spline-rank and empirical-Hessian bound. Consequently the advertised heavy transfer, learned Gaussian branch, moving QTE law, and refitted coverage remain explicit downstream obligations rather than established conclusions. The oracle leading arm vector and an internal raw scalar diagnostic are now defined coherently.

project_justification.gap: Existing regular-overlap and weak-overlap references do not supply the two-endpoint joint-logit spline rank theorem needed here. More basically, the current frozen chart assumptions do not themselves imply that theorem.
project_justification.niche: The intended contribution remains feasible QTE limit and inference theory under weak overlap, but it requires a binary-coherent first stage and a samplewise oracle comparator before moving-law subsampling can be justified.
project_justification.fill: This repair establishes binary coherence, the exact likelihood score and information, preservation of the explicit model witnesses, a corrected bounded-control sanity theorem, the exact Gaussian evaluation variance, joint-logit Riesz algebra, and a permutation-symmetric oracle statistic. It does not claim the uniform feasible limit or coverage theorems until the chart-to-spline rank obstruction is resolved.

body.related_work: Avella-Medina, Davis, and Samorodnitsky provide the observed-true-propensity weak-overlap quantile benchmark; Hirano, Imbens, and Ridder and Firpo provide regular estimated-propensity context. Ma and Wang and Khan and Tamer are retained only as limited-overlap and support-condition background. Knight supplies the classical check-loss decomposition, and Politis, Romano, and Wolf supply general subsampling context; neither proves the paper-specific learned-propensity coupling. Dorn is weak-overlap nuisance-tail context, and Sant'Anna, Song, and Xu is propensity-balance context. No cited result is asserted to establish the open two-endpoint spline theorem, and the raw scalar diagnostic is not attributed to any published method.
body.technical_internal_limitation: Uniform information, signed-Riesz rates, feasible oracle transfer, the learned Gaussian expansion, joint QTE convergence, and refitted pointwise or simultaneous coverage are unproved on the current frozen class. The precise missing ingredient is a uniform lower-rank and empirical-Hessian bound for the two profiled log-chart directions relative to the spatial spline basis. The calculation is valid for the explicit regular charts \(d_1(x)=x\) and \(d_0(x)=1-x\), but the class allows more general measurable charts. The critical fold-law question also remains separate and open.
body.honest_scope: Established in this round are the joint log-odds implication of the former paired links, nonempty mixed and two-heavy witnesses, finite joint Bernoulli information, bounded-control clipping and Hill-classification sanity on the mixed chart under its corrected schedule, exact Gaussian evaluation-variance and Riesz algebra, and permutation symmetry of an explicit oracle leading statistic. The heavy, Gaussian, joint-QTE, and subsampling theorems remain open because the general chart-to-spline rank step is absent. The raw scalar construction is only an internal diagnostic; no negative claim about a published estimator or guarantee is made.
body.interpretation: The joint-logit repair removes the incoherence of separately fitted binary arms and exposes the correct boundary weight \(\pi_0\pi_1\). The remaining failure is not a variance-symbol typo: Hall marginal tails do not control how an arbitrary measurable endpoint chart aligns with quasi-uniform spline cells. Moving-law recombination and complete-subsample algebra are therefore conditional architecture, not current inference guarantees.
